Adams County, OH Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in Ohio
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Selling in Adams County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Adams County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Ohio statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

The Adams County recorder of deeds records Ohio deeds and mortgages. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who records deeds in Adams County

  • Adams County Recorder records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Statewide statutory base recording fee (ORC 317.32): $34 first two pages ($17 base + $17 housing trust fund) and $8 each additional page, plus document preservation surcharge up to $5 deposited to county general fund

Recording and transfer tax

  • The grantor (seller) pays the 319.54(G)(3) fee and any county real property transfer tax levied under ORC Chapter 322 at deed delivery, via statement of value filed with the county auditor. (ORC 319.202(D) (eff. Sept. 30, 2025); source)
  • A deed must be signed by the grantor and the signing acknowledged before a judge or clerk of a court of record, county auditor, county engineer, notary public, or mayor. (ORC 5301.01(A) (eff. Jan. 30, 2014); source)
  • Transfer on death designation affidavits are recorded by the county recorder in the same manner and for the same fee as deeds. (ORC 5302.22(E); source)

Fees

County recording fees change, so we do not quote a total. Check the recorder's current fee schedule before you file.

Selling in Adams County?
We buy Adams County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Treasurer due dates, delinquent/foreclosure info, recorder fee schedule, e-recording, millage not located on official pages
  • Millage not captured: Ohio Dept of Taxation rates25.xlsx (tax.ohio.gov Tax Data Series) failed to scrape

How to sell a house in Adams County

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded deed or the probate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in Ohio.

What a cash sale of a Adams County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Adams County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Ohio disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Adams County

  • Ask the county recorder what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Ohio change, so confirm details with the official office or a Ohio attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Adams County

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Adams County recorder of deeds FAQ

Where do I record a deed in Adams County?

At the county recorder of deeds. Confirm submission rules on the county page.

Do I owe realty transfer tax?

Realty transfer tax can apply to deeds. The Department of Revenue lists the exemptions.

title: Belmont County, OH Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax
content:
Belmont County, OH Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in Ohio
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Selling in Belmont County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Belmont County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Ohio statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

The Belmont County recorder of deeds records Ohio deeds and mortgages. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who records deeds in Belmont County

  • Belmont County Recorder records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Statewide statutory base recording fee (ORC 317.32): $34 first two pages ($17 base + $17 housing trust fund) and $8 each additional page, plus document preservation surcharge up to $5 deposited to county general fund

Recording and transfer tax

  • The grantor (seller) pays the 319.54(G)(3) fee and any county real property transfer tax levied under ORC Chapter 322 at deed delivery, via statement of value filed with the county auditor. (ORC 319.202(D) (eff. Sept. 30, 2025); source)
  • A deed must be signed by the grantor and the signing acknowledged before a judge or clerk of a court of record, county auditor, county engineer, notary public, or mayor. (ORC 5301.01(A) (eff. Jan. 30, 2014); source)
  • Transfer on death designation affidavits are recorded by the county recorder in the same manner and for the same fee as deeds. (ORC 5302.22(E); source)

Fees

County recording fees change, so we do not quote a total. Check the recorder's current fee schedule before you file.

Selling in Belmont County?
We buy Belmont County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • fee schedule, e-recording, millage
  • Millage not captured: Ohio Dept of Taxation rates25.xlsx (tax.ohio.gov Tax Data Series) failed to scrape

How to sell a house in Belmont County

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded deed or the probate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in Ohio.

What a cash sale of a Belmont County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Belmont County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Ohio disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Belmont County

  • Ask the county recorder what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Ohio change, so confirm details with the official office or a Ohio attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Belmont County

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Belmont County recorder of deeds FAQ

Where do I record a deed in Belmont County?

At the county recorder of deeds. Confirm submission rules on the county page.

Do I owe realty transfer tax?

Realty transfer tax can apply to deeds. The Department of Revenue lists the exemptions.

title: Clermont County, OH Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax
content:
Clermont County, OH Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in Ohio
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Selling in Clermont County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Clermont County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Ohio statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

The Clermont County recorder of deeds records Ohio deeds and mortgages. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who records deeds in Clermont County

  • Clermont County Recorder records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Statewide statutory base recording fee (ORC 317.32): $34 first two pages ($17 base + $17 housing trust fund) and $8 each additional page, plus document preservation surcharge up to $5 deposited to county general fund
  • Clermont Recorder accepts electronic (E-Filing) submission; Recorder has Fee Schedule and E-Filing pages (per Auditor 'Filing a Deed' page)

Recording and transfer tax

  • The grantor (seller) pays the 319.54(G)(3) fee and any county real property transfer tax levied under ORC Chapter 322 at deed delivery, via statement of value filed with the county auditor. (ORC 319.202(D) (eff. Sept. 30, 2025); source)
  • A deed must be signed by the grantor and the signing acknowledged before a judge or clerk of a court of record, county auditor, county engineer, notary public, or mayor. (ORC 5301.01(A) (eff. Jan. 30, 2014); source)
  • Transfer on death designation affidavits are recorded by the county recorder in the same manner and for the same fee as deeds. (ORC 5302.22(E); source)

Fees

County recording fees change, so we do not quote a total. Check the recorder's current fee schedule before you file.

Selling in Clermont County?
We buy Clermont County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • due dates, fee schedule, millage
  • Millage not captured: Ohio Dept of Taxation rates25.xlsx (tax.ohio.gov Tax Data Series) failed to scrape

How to sell a house in Clermont County

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded deed or the probate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in Ohio.

What a cash sale of a Clermont County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Clermont County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Ohio disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Clermont County

  • Ask the county recorder what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Ohio change, so confirm details with the official office or a Ohio attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Clermont County

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Clermont County recorder of deeds FAQ

Where do I record a deed in Clermont County?

At the county recorder of deeds. Confirm submission rules on the county page.

Do I owe realty transfer tax?

Realty transfer tax can apply to deeds. The Department of Revenue lists the exemptions.
